title: A queue in 1995: Queue<Card>, std::queue, and a VB array with ReDim
requirements: Three equal columns headed "C#", "C++", "Visual Basic (1995)". Left (C#): `var hand = new Queue<Card>();` / `hand.Enqueue(c);` / `var top = hand.Dequeue();`. Middle: `std::queue<Card> hand;` / `hand.push(c);` / `Card top = hand.front(); hand.pop();`. Right: the real program's approach, quoted from Program.vb (the `Hand` structure with `Cards()` and `Count`, and the `ReDim`/shift), marked as the excerpt it is.
The point on screen: two languages have a queue; VB has an array and a counter. A one-line footer: "No generic collections, no built-in queue: an array and a counter."
